method: Root physically viewed all17 original whole simulator frames. No crop, measurement, tracing, masks, alignment or pixel-derived geometry. Selection/orbit/binary assertions are separately retained in automation receipts.
findings: The oak body uses the shared wood finish, while the isolated insert has a dark speckled granite finish. Only the selected contact turns red.
Granite returns to its speckled finish in the same live scene after the wood hold is selected, and remains correct after a real orbit.
Front and reverse side orbits show the cord following the longitudinal side seat and turning into the middle side opening; all three transverse adjustment notches on each visible side are retained.
The support loop is short relative to the board. Both exposed leads run taut to the apex and remain seated along the side.
All eight selected rims or granite floors appear below their cavity in the selected hanging orientation; the native proof separately verifies upward-bearing directions.
Five actual drag actions preserve the selection and change projected contact frames. No conspicuous mesh gaps, floating highlights or unstable cord departures appear in these still frames.
cosmeticLimits: Small polygonal shading bands remain at the tight cord bend where it meets the side seat; these are visible in the side frame and do not change the route.
Wood and granite are the app finishes. Exact groove sizes, cord dimensions/support height and hidden passage continuation are display estimates or unknown, as recorded in the native/source packet.
Still frames and the recorded drag states do not establish behavior at every continuous camera angle.
